101

You will explore different ways to work in Grok Build, use modes and models for the right tasks, apply rules and skills to ensure consistent quality, and complete at least one task with an agent.

What is Grok Build? How do you work with an agent? How do you govern an agent?

What is Grok Build?

Ask

  • Let’s learn more about the application with Ask mode.
Paste in Grok Build 
/ask Tell me what this application does in 3 sentences

Plan

  • Map your approach to building a new feature in Plan mode.
Paste in Grok Build 
/plan I want a new feature to update the customer email in the invoice detail customer card. Don’t implement email validation.

Build in Agent mode

  • Build the feature in Agent mode. Build the plan locally. Check the feature in the UI.

Debug

  • Investigate the failing test using Debug mode. Debug mode is useful because the agent investigates the codebase and presents some hypothesis on the root cause. I can choose to reproduce the bug and attempt to fix based on the agent’s hypotheses.
Paste in Grok Build 
/debug the failing test

Check the models

  • Check the models available for use. Select Auto in the chat and review the models available for use.

Plan to fix the bug

  • Use shift-tab to toggle to Agent mode.
Paste in Grok Build 
Fix the failing test.

How do you work with an agent?

Run Mode Allowlist

  • Let’s change how our agent asks for approvals by configuring an allowlist - a known set of commands that Grok Build can run without asking for review. Go to Settings > Agents > Executions & Approvals > Run Mode > Allowlist.

Verify the email feature

  • Go to http://localhost:43173/invoices/inv_1048. Find the edit email feature you implemented in the Customer box.

Redact (partial)

Paste in Grok Build 
Redact the customer email in the UI. The first two characters and domain are plaintext. When I click to type in the box, clear it and save the new email.

Stop the prompt

  • Stop the prompt with the Stop button in the chat.

Interrupt and steer

  • Steer the prompt. Show how the agent pauses for your approval. Continue running after reviewing the first file.
Paste in Grok Build 
Redact the customer email in the UI. Show it in plaintext when I click the box to edit it. Stop every time you change a file for me to review.

Continue to the end

Paste in Grok Build 
Continue to the end, do not wait for my approval.

Review diffs

  • Select Changes in the right hand panel. Show diffs from agent’s last turn.

Restore from a checkpoint

  • If I want to revert the code, I can restore from a checkpoint. Scroll back to a prompt before updating the feature. Select the restore icon next to the prompt.

How do you govern an agent?

Create a user rule

  • Let’s create a user rule so the agent doesn’t try to improve the invoice UI without our approval. Use /create-rule, a built-in skill, to create a rule. Go to Customize > Rules > User to view the rule.
Paste in Grok Build 
/create-rule Preserve the invoice view. Do not rename, restyle, or rearrange invoice screens unless the user names the **exact** new copy (or a specific layout change). This is a personal rule.

Test the rule

Paste in Grok Build 
Change "Line Items" in the UI to something else.

Create a user skill

  • Let’s create a user skill that tells me the domain breakdown and available APIs. Go to Customize > Skills to view the skill.
Paste in Grok Build 
/create-skill Use domain-driven design to break down the domains in this application and match it to available APIs or data schemas. This is a personal skill.

Test the skill

Paste in Grok Build 
Use domain-driven design on this application. Do not edit files.

Canvas

  • Use Canvas to generate interactive artifacts that render next to the chat.
Paste in Grok Build 
Create a canvas explaining what we did today.

MCP / Figma

  • Ask Grok Build to create a slideshow in Figma using MCP Servers. Find an MCP server for slideshow generation in Grok Build. Go to Customize > MCPs > Figma.
Paste in Grok Build 
Create three slides in Figma Slides outlining how I used Grok Build to develop a new feature. I want to use this as part of my demo showcase.

201

You will curate what belongs in an agent's context, encode conventions as project skills, connect a curated set of MCP servers, and split one task across parallel agents.

How do you manage context? How do you standardize agents? How do you connect external tools? How do you parallelize a task?

How do you manage context?

Open one agent and ask it for information about the entire codebase.

Paste in Grok Build 
/rename-chat Agent 1 All

Ask DDD of the application

Paste in Grok Build 
/ask what is the domain driven design of the application.

Let’s open a second agent. This starts a new context window.

Paste in Grok Build 
/rename-chat Agent 2 Target

Ask DDD of the invoice table

Paste in Grok Build 
/ask what is the domain driven design of the @invoice-table.tsx

Check agent 1’s context window.

  • Go to Agent 1 All chat. Click the Context Usage indicator below the chat. Agent 1 maps all the domains in the whole codebase. Its context window shows X%.

Check agent 2’s context window.

  • Go to Agent 2 Target. Click the Context Usage indicator below the chat. Agent 2 maps half of the domains based on the targeted context. Its context window shows Y%. The difference in context window may not be significant but can affect larger repositories.

We want to check if the invoice table can be changed in isolation.

  • Agent 1 did the work of identifying all domains. Agent 2 can benefit from its summary. It doesn’t need to review the entire codebase again. Go to Agent 2 Target chat.
Paste in Grok Build 
/ask @Agent 1 All Does refactoring the table change anything across all contexts?

How do you standardize agents?

Open a new agent and add a new personal skill.

  • Open a new agent. Every time I ask a new agent to create an API, it forgets how to do it and scans the entire repository for the pattern. Let’s create a skill for it so the agent can do less work. Open skill in ~/.cursor/skills.
Paste in Grok Build 
/create-skill for how to create a new API. Follow the standards in this repo. This is a personal skill named create-api.

Create a project skill.

  1. A teammate mentioned they were frustrated because they had to keep correcting the agent when it builds the API. They asked if they could also use the API skill.
  2. Open skill in .cursor/skills
  3. Review the other project skills for this repository, such as add-dashboard-widget, draft-collection-email, or write-prisma-query.
Paste in Grok Build 
Promote the create-api skill to this project.

How do you orchestrate agents?

Plan the command center on a Cloud Agent.

This plan runs on a remote machine, so it keeps going while I do the keyboard walkthrough locally.

  • Start a new Cloud Agent.
Paste in Grok Build 
/plan the collections command center from its open Linear issues. List the tasks, the files each touches, and the open questions.

Get the issues for the collections command center from the issue tracker.

The Linear MCP server returns a list of nine issues to create the collections command center.

  • Start a new local agent.
Paste in Grok Build 
/ask List open issues for the collections command center in Linear.

Plan the collections command center in a separate agent.

We are going to run this first and handle the manual part in parallel. This agent only plans. It builds nothing until we come back to it.

Paste in Grok Build 
/plan the collections command center from its issues. List the tasks, the files each touches, and the open questions.

Start a keyboard walkthrough for the accessibility audit in a new agent.

  • Start a new local agent for the keyboard walkthrough.

Show the problem by hand.

Focus is the control the keyboard is on right now. When you press Tab, focus moves to the next button, link, or field. A visible outline usually shows where it is, so a keyboard user always knows what Enter will do. Pressing Tab repeatedly is a slow manual process. Is there a way we can automate this?

  1. Open Browser to http://localhost:43173/invoices.
  2. Press Tab a few times on the invoices page.

Build a subagent to help automate the manual process.

CI catches missing labels, which break screen readers, and low contrast, which makes text hard to read. A keyboard walkthrough takes judgment, so this subagent uses the page the way a keyboard user would. Reuse it any time you change the UI.

Paste in Grok Build 
/create-subagent accessibility-manual-reviewer that walks pages by keyboard in the Browser, since CI runs automated tests. Report tab order, focus, trap, Escape, and navigation failures with screenshots. Set model: fast, readonly: false.
  • npm run demo:session -- record project-path .cursor/agents/accessibility-manual-reviewer.md

Start a new agent to audit accessibility.

A new agent keeps the audit separate from the command center plan.

  • Start a new local agent.

Show /multitask for small coordinated jobs.

The coordinator gives each task its own subagent: a keyboard walkthrough of the invoices page, the accessibility test suite, and the application test suite.

  • Open Browser to http://localhost:43173/invoices.
Paste in Grok Build 
/multitask Split into three subagents: accessibility-manual-reviewer checks @components/notice-bell.tsx on the invoices page (click, Tab once, Escape, stop at one failure), one runs accessibility tests, one runs app tests.

Review the subagents.

Stop one task if it drifts. When each agent completes, you get a set of recommendations.

  • Watch the Working indicator above the chat box.

Check the output of the subagents.

The coordinator summarizes the failures from the keyboard walkthrough of the invoices page, the accessibility test suite, and the application test suite.

Paste in Grok Build 
Give me a one-sentence summary for each subagent.

Fallback: reference repo issues

  • If an agent cannot access the Linear MCP server, use the issue descriptions in the repository.
Paste in Grok Build 
Reference issues from @runbooks/linear-field-demos.ts instead of Linear.

How do you go from plan to code?

Start a new Project.

Starting a new Project creates a long-running Cloud Agent that acts as a coordinator. Run the remaining commands in the Project. Note that responses to prompts may differ from responses in an individual agent.

  1. Start a new Project.
  2. Name it {{ INSERT COMPANY HERE, default is Ledgerly }}.

Stage the Project.

Make clear to the Project that each agent runs in its own worktree to isolate work and avoid conflicts.

Paste in Grok Build 
Run each agent in its own worktree to avoid conflicts, and parallelize where possible.

Use Projects to assign tasks to agents.

Let Projects decide how best to assign tasks and complete work.

  • Run the remaining prompts in this demo section from the Project without starting new agents.

Start a new agent.

I want to fix the keyboard findings that do not share a file.

  • Open a new local agent.

Start a plan to fix the walkthrough failures on a separate worktree.

Plan the in-scope findings, one task per finding, each on its own worktree. If the plan asks questions, choose to run tasks in parallel and write updates to the issue tracker. By starting the work on a separate worktree, you avoid editing the working code on the main branch. If you do not let the agent automatically approve changes on the worktree, you may have to manually approve each file change.

Paste in Grok Build 
/plan the in-scope keyboard fixes in @.cursor/plans/keyboard-walkthrough-audit.md. One task per finding, in parallel, each on its own worktree with auto-approved changes.

Review the plan.

The plan assigns tasks to workers and notes which ones run in parallel.

  • Review the plan.

Build the plan.

  • Click Build Locally.

Use Cloud Agents to build the plan if you do not have Projects.

  • Build the plan with Cloud Agents.

Ask a side question while the coordinator remediates the findings.

Paste in Grok Build 
/side

Ask what the first subagent is remediating.

If you want to know what a subagent is doing, you can open a side chat and ask without blocking the coordinator.

Paste in Grok Build 
/ask What is the first subagent remediating? Answer with the finding and the files it changes.

Consolidate and open a reviewable PR.

Move finished worktrees back deliberately. Resolve conflicts on purpose.

  • Open the PR. Show the summary a coworker would read first.
Paste in Grok Build 
Consolidate the completed tasks into one branch so reviewers get one PR. Open a PR with what each task changed and what a human should verify.

Keep track of the Project.

As you continue working on the Project, it keeps track of your requests to agents. You can review tasks in project notes and shared files in context.

Paste in Grok Build 
Show me the project notes and context.

How do you scale review?

Start a new agent.

With many lines of accessibility fixes in this PR, I want to identify the most important files to review.

  • Open a new local agent.
Paste in Grok Build 
Check out the branch for the keyboard fixes PR.

Run the change reviewer subagent before you conduct manual review.

The change reviewer uses readonly: false so it can run git diff, but its instructions stop it from editing files. The reviewer and the author stay separate.

Paste in Grok Build 
Use the change reviewer subagent to review the remediation PR. List each issue with its file, line, and severity.

Identify any changes requiring closer inspection.

The plan includes a step that sounds reasonable but blocks Tab navigation everywhere. The change reviewer flags it as high severity, with the file and line, so we never keep it.

  • Check the change reviewer’s output for any issues requiring closer inspection.
Paste in Grok Build 
Fix the findings from the change reviewer.

Review the high-risk changes.

The change reviewer subagent clears the noise so your time goes where judgment matters.

  • Open the highest-risk change and read it line by line.
Paste in Grok Build 
/ask Which change in this PR has the highest risk? List the files and lines I need to review.

Run Bugbot.

Run Bugbot to check for code quality. Review its suggestions for changes.

Paste in Grok Build 
/review-bugbot this remediation PR

How do you share ownership safely?

Start a new agent.

I want to turn some of the review findings in this PR into the most reliable fix: a rule, skill, subagent, test, or human check.

  • Open a new local agent.

Identify the most reliable fix for each review finding.

You choose which ones to turn into a rule, skill, subagent, test, or human check for your coworkers to reuse.

Paste in Grok Build 
Turn repeat findings from this PR's review comments and change reviewer into reusable fixes so they stop recurring. Draft the most deterministic fix for each: a rule, skill, subagent, test, or human check.

Create an Automation.

  1. Go to the Automations tab.
  2. Click New Automation.
  3. Name it Reviewer.
  4. Select the demo repository.
  5. Click Triggers > PR opened, then select the demo repository and set the author to Anyone.
  6. Add “Use the change reviewer subagent to review this PR and comment with each issue's file, line, and severity.” to agent instructions.
  7. Add “Comment on Pull Request” to tools.
  8. Click Save.

Trigger the PR Automation.

Opening any PR triggers the Reviewer Automation, so I'll create one and watch the check run.

  1. Start a new local agent.
  2. Open the PR for the accessibility test suite fixes and review the status check for Automation: Reviewer.
Paste in Grok Build 
Run the accessibility test suite and fix its failures on a separate worktree. Open a PR when done.
